thread:
sam.k: Quick check — discovered a discrepancy between Python SDK and TS SDK when calling /v1/generate. Python sends {\"temperature\": 0.7} while TS sends {\"temp\": 0.7}. REST accepts temperature but our TS SDK tests are failing in some back-compat checks.

amy.peters: Ugh, of course. Do we have a canonical mapping doc? I thought we standardized on snake_case in the REST body.

luca: REST expects the full field name 'temperature'. SDKs should map any alias client-side for ergonomics but send the canonical REST key. TS should be doing mapping already, weird.

jen: Can you paste request examples from both SDKs?

sam.k: Sure — Python payload we send (working):
```json
{"model":"rwd-16b","prompt":"hi","temperature":0.7}
```
TS payload (from tests):
```json
{"model":"rwd-16b","prompt":"hi","temp":0.7}
```

chip: Also seeing cases where TS includes undefined keys as null in the serialized JSON when a param is omitted — that breaks servers that validate strictly. Example: TS client does JSON.stringify({stop: undefined}) -> {} normally, but our helper sometimes turns undefined -> null. Need to find where.

sdk-bot: Note: CI failing for SDK-TS: test 238 - request schema validation error.

amy.peters: Another wrinkle — REST previously accepted both string and array for 'stop' (backcompat), Python always normalizes to array, TS sometimes sends a string when caller passes single string. Do we want server to accept both or enforce array?

luca: We should keep server permissive for a release or two. But SDKs should normalize to the canonical shape. So: temperature (float), stop (array of strings), max_output_tokens (int). TS should map 'maxTokens' and 'max_tokens' -> 'max_output_tokens'.

jen: Action items: 1) Add mapping layer in TS serializer to rename aliases to canonical names. 2) Add unit serialization tests to ensure undefined is omitted and null is never emitted for absent optional fields. 3) Update server validation to accept string|array for 'stop' for one major release, then tighten.

sam.k: I'm happy to open the TS PR for (1) and (2). Quick question on naming: current REST uses 'max_output_tokens' but Python SDK exposes 'max_tokens'. Which should TS expose?

chip: Expose what users expect: 'max_tokens' (both SDKs) map to 'max_output_tokens' in the REST payload. Keep ergonomics stable. Add deprecation note in changelog for direct usage of 'max_output_tokens' in SDKs.

amy.peters: Also add a tiny e2e that hits a staging gateway where server validates the canonical keys. That will catch regressions like the 'temp' leak.

luca: For the undefined->null bug: look at our object-assign helper in ts/sdk/src/serialize.ts — it currently does Object.keys(map).reduce and sets value ?? null in one branch. That's the culprit. Replace with conditional set: if (v !== undefined) out[k] = v.

jen: Great catch. Sam, if you can open the PR today label it 'hotfix/serialization' and request review from @luca and @amy. I'll add the test matrix to the SDK CI job for both Python and TS.

sam.k: Will do. Drafting PR now. I'll include failing test snippets and a before/after of payload.

amy.peters: For the server side, I'll relax 'stop' validation for the next two releases and add a small regression test. Also adding a telemetry metric when we receive non-canonical keys so we can measure how many clients use aliases. :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

chip: +1. Also create a tiny migration note for customers relying on shorthand keys.

jen: OK team — summary: TS PR to normalize aliases -> canonical keys + fix undefined/null serialization (sam). Python: add e2e and changelog note (jen). Server: accept string|array for 'stop' and telemetry for aliases (amy). Follow-up sync if there are deployment regressions.

sam.k: Thanks — pinging in PR when ready. :thumbsup:

sdk-bot: CI queued for branch hotfix/serialization by sam.k (build 204).
